findings.title: Monolithic App component with excessive route-specific knowledge
findings.description: lib/public/js/app.js acts as a god component: it owns location parsing for /agents, /chat, /cron, /envars, /models, /nodes, manually checks isXRoute booleans, extracts selectedAgentId/selectedCronJobId via regex, and mounts route components conditionally outside the Switch. This bypasses wouter-preact's routing for most routes, duplicates routing logic, and creates a tight coupling between the shell and every feature. Adding a new route requires editing this 400+ line file in multiple places (booleans, regex parsers, JSX branches, sidebar handlers).
findings.recommendation: Move all route mounting into the <Switch> with <Route> declarations and use route params (via wouter useParams) instead of regex parsing of location. Extract sidebar wiring into a separate AppShell component and let each route component own its own pane wrapper class.

findings.title: Inconsistent routing strategy: hand-rolled conditionals bypass Switch/Route
findings.description: Some routes (/general, /doctor, /telegram, /usage, /webhooks, /watchdog) are declared inside <Switch> with proper <Route> elements, while /agents, /chat, /cron, /envars, /models, /nodes are mounted via plain conditional rendering using location.startsWith(). This dual routing model means route precedence, fallthrough, and the catch-all <RouteRedirect to="/general"> behave unpredictably, and the lib/public/js/components/routes/index.js barrel exports become inconsistently used.
findings.recommendation: Pick one routing strategy (recommend wouter <Switch>/<Route>) and migrate all panes into it. The barrel in components/routes/index.js already exports route components — use them uniformly inside the Switch.

findings.title: Cross-cutting global window state and DOM events used as control plane
findings.description: The shell uses window['__alphaclawPendingCreateAgent'] as a flag to coordinate navigation→action handoff, dispatches CustomEvents on window ('alphaclaw:create-agent'), and listens for them in components/agents-tab/index.js. This is an ad-hoc pub/sub bypassing the component tree, making data flow opaque and racy. Window globals also pollute the namespace ('__alphaclawSetupAppBootCount').
findings.recommendation: Replace window-flag + window.dispatchEvent with explicit prop callbacks or a small typed event bus / context. Pass an onRequestCreateAgent prop down to AgentsRoute and trigger the modal via state, removing the need for cross-tree DOM events.

findings.title: Plugin tightly coupled to undocumented core event names and ctx shape
findings.description: lib/plugin/usage-tracker/index.js subscribes to 'llm_output' and 'tool_result_persist' events with hand-coded shapes for event.usage.{input,output,cacheRead,cacheWrite,total} and ctx.{sessionId,sessionKey,toolName}. There is no shared schema/contract module visible — the plugin will silently break (writes 0) if the host changes field names. This violates the typical plugin-architecture contract of stable, documented hooks.
findings.recommendation: Define the plugin API surface in a shared module (e.g. lib/server/plugin-api/contracts.js) exporting event name constants, event shape validators, and version. Have the plugin import constants instead of hardcoding strings, and version-check the api object on register.

findings.title: Plugin opens its own SQLite DB and resolves config out-of-band
findings.description: The usage-tracker plugin independently resolves the install root from process.env (ALPHACLAW_ROOT_DIR / OPENCLAW_HOME / OPENCLAW_ROOT_DIR / homedir fallback) and opens its own SQLite file. The host server presumably already knows the config root and may manage other DBs. Each plugin reinventing path resolution leads to inconsistencies (which env wins?) and bypasses any centralized DB lifecycle (close on shutdown, migrations, backup).
findings.recommendation: Have the host pass an api.paths.dataDir (or api.openDatabase('usage')) to plugin.register() so plugins do not duplicate environment resolution. Centralize DB connection lifecycle in the host so close()/WAL checkpointing happens on shutdown.

findings.title: No DB connection close / lifecycle hook in plugin
findings.description: The plugin lazily opens DatabaseSync on first event but never exposes an unregister/close hook. On server reload or shutdown the WAL file may not checkpoint cleanly, prepared statements leak, and tests cannot tear down the plugin between runs. The plugin contract appears to expose only register(api) with no symmetric dispose.
findings.recommendation: Extend the plugin contract to support an optional unregister/dispose function that closes prepared statements and the DatabaseSync handle. Have the host call it during shutdown.

findings.title: App component drills 20+ props into AppSidebar — missing context boundary
findings.description: AppSidebar receives ~25 props (mobileSidebarOpen, authEnabled, menuRef, navSections, agents, selectedAgentId, chatSessions, selectedChatSessionKey, callbacks, ...). This prop drilling is a classic indicator of a missing context/provider seam between the shell and feature areas. Any sidebar contract change ripples through App, useAppShellUi, useAppShellController, useBrowseNavigation, and useAgents.
findings.recommendation: Introduce focused contexts: AppShellContext (sidebar/menu state), NavigationContext (location, browse), AgentSelectionContext (agents, selectedAgentId), ChatSessionContext. AppSidebar then consumes contexts directly rather than receiving everything as props.

findings.title: Defensive duplicate-bootstrap clear masks an architectural issue
findings.description: The bootstrap code increments window.__alphaclawSetupAppBootCount and calls render(null, ...) + replaceChildren() before the real render to defend against duplicate App instantiations. A counter and forced clear suggests script tags or module re-execution paths are firing twice, which is an architectural problem (likely double-include or HMR misconfiguration) rather than something to be papered over at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Identify why bootstrap runs more than once (duplicate <script> tag, HMR, SSR rehydration). Fix the include path/bundling and remove the defensive clear; if a guard is genuinely needed, use a single window-level boolean rather than an incrementing counter.

findings.title: Server architecture files referenced in plan not provided — relying on inferred boundaries
findings.description: The PLAN highlighted lib/server.js, lib/server/init/*, lib/server/agents/service.js, lib/server/gateway.js, lib/server/startup.js as the core targets for backend layering analysis, but only the usage-tracker plugin and frontend files were included. Findings are therefore concentrated on frontend shell architecture and the plugin contract; backend layer-violation/circular-dependency assessment cannot be confirmed from evidence.
findings.recommendation: Re-run analysis with lib/server.js, lib/server/init/, lib/server/routes/, lib/server/agents/service.js, and lib/server/gateway.js included to assess routes/services/db separation and SSE/WS coordination.

findings.title: OAuth popup auth URL constructed without verifying same-origin postMessage source
findings.description: In lib/public/js/components/google/index.js the message handler accepts event.data.google === 'success'/'error' from any window without checking event.origin. Although same-origin policy makes injecting messages from cross-origin frames difficult, it is best practice to verify origin to prevent confused-deputy issues if a malicious page is opened in the same browser context. CWE-346: Origin Validation Error.
findings.recommendation: In the window 'message' event handler, add: if (event.origin !== window.location.origin) return; before processing event.data. Also validate that event.source matches the popup window reference returned by window.open.

findings.title: SQL composed with template literals in usage-tracker (low risk, no user input)
findings.description: lib/plugin/usage-tracker/index.js uses database.exec with template-literal SQL strings for schema creation and ALTER TABLE statements. The strings are static and contain no user input, so there is no SQL injection risk. The data-write paths correctly use prepared statements with named parameters. This is informational only — pattern is safe as written but worth flagging because future maintainers might add interpolation. CWE-89 (not currently exploitable).
findings.recommendation: Add a comment indicating these schema strings must remain literal. Continue using prepared statements (already done correctly via database.prepare with $named parameters) for all dynamic queries.

findings.title: Test files not provided despite being primary focus area
findings.description: The PLAN explicitly listed tests/server/, tests/frontend/, and vitest.config.js as primary focus files, but no test files were included in the analyzed code. This prevents validation of test coverage breadth across routes and services, integration vs unit test balance, and frontend hook testability claims. The lib/server/agents/service.js, lib/server/cron-service.js, and lib/server/doctor/service.js files mentioned in the plan were also not provided.
findings.recommendation: Provide test files and core service modules to enable meaningful coverage analysis. Without these, coverage and complexity claims for the focus areas cannot be verified.

findings.title: Massive App component with excessive responsibilities (~470 lines)
findings.description: The App component in lib/public/js/app.js spans roughly 470 lines and orchestrates onboarding, sidebar, routing for 15+ routes, browse navigation, agent selection, chat sessions, doctor warnings, and UI settings persistence. It composes 5 hooks, contains 3 useEffects with mixed concerns, 3 inline IIFE regex parsers for route params, and renders an enormous JSX tree. Cyclomatic complexity is high due to 7+ ternary route guards (isAgentsRoute, isChatRoute, isCronRoute, etc.) interleaved in a single render.
findings.recommendation: Extract a RouteSwitcher component for the route ternaries, move route param derivation (selectedAgentId, agentDetailTab, selectedCronJobId) into a useRouteParams hook, and split the StatusBar/MobileTopbar into separate components. Target App < 150 lines.

findings.title: DoctorTab component exceeds 400 lines with deeply nested ternary rendering
findings.description: lib/public/js/components/doctor/index.js DoctorTab is over 450 lines with 4 useEffects containing complex dependency-driven state synchronization (selectedRunFilter reset logic, pendingRunSelectionId reconciliation), 14+ useMemo/derived values, and multi-level nested ternary template rendering (showInitialLoadingState ? ... : hasRuns ? ... ). The reconciliation logic between activeRunId, pendingRunSelectionId, and selectedRunFilter is particularly hard to follow.
findings.recommendation: Extract a useDoctorRunSelection hook to encapsulate run filter reconciliation. Move banner/empty-state/findings panels into separate sub-components. Replace nested ternaries with early returns or a switch on a derived view-state enum.

findings.title: FileViewer renders 7-deep nested ternary for content display
findings.description: FileViewer's main render uses a 7-level nested ternary (loading ? ... : error ? ... : isImage/Audio ? ... : isSqlite ? ... : isDiff ? ... : isMarkdown ? ... : default) which is hard to scan and modify. Each branch passes 10+ props down. This pattern impedes adding new file types and complicates testing of individual rendering paths.
findings.recommendation: Replace nested ternaries with a renderContent() function using early returns, or build a viewer registry mapping file-type predicates to components. Reduces complexity and makes each viewer independently testable.

findings.title: Google component has 18+ state variables and 12+ handlers in one file
findings.description: lib/public/js/components/google/index.js has 18+ pieces of useState and useMemo state (expandedAccountId, scopesByAccountId, savedScopesByAccountId, apiStatusByAccountId, checkingByAccountId, addMenuOpen, credentialsModalState, addCompanyModalOpen, savingAddCompany, disconnectAccountId, gmailWizardState, etc.) plus 12+ handlers (startAuth, handleToggleScope, handleCheckApis, handleDisconnect, openCredentialsModal, closeCredentialsModal, handleCredentialsSaved, handleAddCompanyAccount, handleAddCompanyClick, handleAddPersonalClick, handleEditCredentials, handleEnableGmailWatch, handleDisableGmailWatch, handleFinishGmailSetupWizard). This god-component pattern hurts testability.
findings.recommendation: Extract a useGoogleAccountActions hook covering credential modal state and auth flows; extract a useApiStatusChecker hook for the apiStatus/checking maps. Move handleAddCompanyAccount/handleAddCompanyClick into the existing useGoogleAccounts hook.

findings.title: Silent error swallowing in catch blocks
findings.description: Multiple catch blocks silently swallow errors with empty bodies, hiding failures that could indicate genuine bugs. In app.js: `try { window.localStorage.clear(); ... } catch {}`. In telegram-workspace/index.js: `} catch {}` appears in 6 places (loadTelegramWorkspaceState, save/remove variants, bootstrapWorkspace). In agents-tab/index.js handleEdit silently returns on error after handleUpdateAgent already toasted. This pattern obscures real failures during incident response.
findings.recommendation: At minimum, log errors via console.warn or a logger. Distinguish between expected errors (e.g., JSON.parse on missing key) and unexpected ones. Avoid blanket `catch {}`.

findings.title: Inline IIFE regex parsers duplicated for route param extraction
findings.description: app.js uses three separate inline IIFEs to parse route params from `location` (selectedAgentId, agentDetailTab, selectedCronJobId), each running on every render. This is duplicated logic that should live in a hook. Each IIFE re-runs the regex per render even when location is unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Create useRouteParams(location) hook returning memoized { selectedAgentId, agentDetailTab, selectedCronJobId }. Use useMemo with location dependency to avoid re-parsing.

findings.title: Global window flag used as cross-component event signaling
findings.description: `window[kPendingCreateAgentWindowFlag]` is used in app.js to coordinate "open create-agent modal after navigation" with agents-tab (which listens for `alphaclaw:create-agent` event). This global mutable state is hard to test, can leak between hot-reloads, and creates implicit coupling. Combined with the `__alphaclawSetupAppBootCount` and the comment "Defensive: clear root so duplicate bootstraps cannot stack full app shells", this signals fragile bootstrap semantics.
findings.recommendation: Replace global flag with a query param or state passed via setLocation, or use a centralized event-bus module that can be mocked in tests. Document and remove the duplicate-bootstrap defense once root cause is fixed.

findings.title: Variable shadowing in CronTab makes code confusing
findings.description: In lib/public/js/components/cron-tab/index.js, `selectedJob` is destructured from state (line 18), then a different `selectedJob` is declared inside useMemo (line 23) shadowing the outer reference. While JS scoping handles this correctly, it's confusing to maintainers and a likely source of future bugs.
findings.recommendation: Rename the inner variable to `matchingJob` or `jobForLabel` to eliminate the shadow.

findings.title: Hardcoded version string and URLs scattered across components
findings.description: lib/public/js/components/nodes-tab/browser-attach/index.js hardcodes `kReleaseNotesUrl = "https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.3.13"` and the markdown contains "OpenClaw 2026.3.13+" requirement text. These will become stale on every release. Similar hardcoded URLs in app.js status bar (docs.openclaw.ai, discord, github).
findings.recommendation: Centralize URLs and version requirements in a config module (e.g., lib/public/js/lib/external-links.js) and inject the current version dynamically rather than hardcoding 2026.3.13 in markdown.

findings.title: ConnectedNodesCard render function has high cyclomatic complexity
findings.description: lib/public/js/components/nodes-tab/connected-nodes/index.js renders nodes with a deeply nested ternary chain: `loading ? ... : error ? ... : !nodes.length ? ... : html\`...\`` plus per-node conditional rendering for browser status, attach state, pending pairs, and reconnect command (8+ conditional branches per node). The map callback alone is ~150 lines.
findings.recommendation: Extract `<NodeCard>` and `<NodeBrowserStatusPanel>` components. The map callback should fit in a few lines. Consider a derived view-state object computed once per node.

findings.title: Schema migration logic uses fragile string-matching for error detection
findings.description: In lib/plugin/usage-tracker/index.js, safeAlterTable() catches errors and checks `message.includes("duplicate column name")` to decide if it's safe to ignore. This is locale/version-dependent and could silently swallow legitimate errors if SQLite changes its error wording. There's no test coverage signal for this fallback path.
findings.recommendation: Check column existence via PRAGMA table_info() before ALTER, rather than relying on error message strings. Add a unit test for the schema migration path.

findings.title: Markdown content embedded as multi-line template literal in JS source
findings.description: lib/public/js/components/nodes-tab/browser-attach/index.js embeds 30+ lines of setup instruction markdown directly in a JS template literal, mixing content with code. This makes the content hard to edit (no markdown syntax highlighting), translate, or version separately, and inflates the bundle.
findings.recommendation: Move setup instructions to a .md file and load via fetch, or use a build-time import. This also enables easier review of doc changes by non-developers.

findings.title: Plugin module lacks file-level documentation and JSDoc
findings.description: The usage-tracker plugin (lib/plugin/usage-tracker/index.js) is a substantial module that creates SQLite schemas, registers event handlers, and is loaded as part of plugin infrastructure. There is no top-of-file comment explaining the plugin contract (what events it consumes, what tables it writes, what the consuming Usage UI expects), and no JSDoc on the public functions like createPlugin, ensureSchema, writeUsageEvent, or writeToolEvent. New contributors must read the entire file to understand the plugin lifecycle and database schema.
findings.recommendation: Add a header block describing the plugin's purpose, the events it listens to (llm_output, tool_result_persist), the tables it manages (usage_events, usage_daily, tool_events), and the env vars that control storage location (ALPHACLAW_ROOT_DIR, OPENCLAW_HOME, OPENCLAW_ROOT_DIR). Add JSDoc to register, writeUsageEvent, and writeToolEvent with @param and @returns annotations.

findings.title: Database schema and env-var precedence undocumented
findings.description: resolveRootDir() falls back through ALPHACLAW_ROOT_DIR, OPENCLAW_HOME, OPENCLAW_ROOT_DIR, and ~/.alphaclaw. This precedence is significant for ops/onboarding (it controls where usage.db is written) but is not commented in the source nor (per the plan) covered in setup/install docs. Similarly, the SQLite schema (usage_events, usage_daily, tool_events) and the column-add migration via safeAlterTable are undocumented — anyone querying the Usage UI's DB will need to reverse-engineer the schema.
findings.recommendation: Document the env-var precedence inline above resolveRootDir and surface it in README/AGENTS.md install docs. Add a schema reference (markdown table or doc/usage-db.md) describing each table, column, and migration. Inline-comment safeAlterTable to clarify it is idempotent for adding session_key.

findings.title: Hash-router routes have no central documentation
findings.description: lib/public/js/app.js declares the entire client-side route map (/general, /doctor, /telegram/:accountId, /providers, /watchdog, /usage, /usage/:sessionId, /webhooks, /webhooks/:hookName, /agents, /chat, /cron, /envars, /models, /nodes, /browse) inline in the App component. The plan explicitly flagged 'API/route documentation absence'. There is no routes table in README.md, AGENTS.md, or a dedicated doc that lists routes, params, and which component handles each. This is a significant onboarding gap for contributors building new tabs or linking deep URLs.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Routes' section to README.md or create docs/routes.md enumerating every hash route, its params, the component that renders it, and required state (e.g., onboarded). Optionally add a JSDoc block at the top of app.js summarizing the route table and the hash-router contract (useHashLocation).

findings.title: Public Preact components lack prop documentation
findings.description: Many exported components accept large prop bags with default destructuring (e.g., AgentBindingsSection, AgentOverview, AgentToolsPanel, AgentsTab, CronTab, DoctorTab, FileViewer, GeneralTab, Google, Models, NodesTab, NodesSetupWizard, TelegramWorkspace) but none have JSDoc/TSDoc for their props. Defaults like onSetLocation = () => {} hint at the contract but say nothing about expected shapes (e.g., agent, agents, workspaceConfig, connectInfo, statusData). This forces consumers to read implementation to know what to pass.
findings.recommendation: Add JSDoc @typedef definitions for shared shapes (Agent, ChannelStatus, GatewayConnectInfo, DoctorStatus, etc.) and JSDoc blocks above each exported component listing each @param prop with type and purpose. Even a 5-line block per component would dramatically improve discoverability.

findings.title: Magic constants and window flags lack explanation
findings.description: lib/public/js/app.js defines kPendingCreateAgentWindowFlag = '__alphaclawPendingCreateAgent', appBootCounter = '__alphaclawSetupAppBootCount', and the custom event 'alphaclaw:create-agent' (also dispatched from agents-tab/index.js). These cross-component coupling points have no comments explaining why they exist (e.g., why a window flag is needed instead of state, why the boot counter is incremented). The 'Defensive: clear root...' comment is good — extend that pattern.
findings.recommendation: Add a comment block near the constants explaining the pending-create-agent flow (set in onAddAgent, consumed by useEffect in App, dispatched as a custom event handled in AgentsTab). Document the 'alphaclaw:*' custom event namespace in a single place (e.g., a doc/events.md or top-of-file comment).

findings.title: BrowserAttachCard contains hard-coded version-specific docs that will drift
findings.description: lib/public/js/components/nodes-tab/browser-attach/index.js embeds a setup/troubleshooting markdown string with a hard-coded release URL (v2026.3.13) and version requirement ('OpenClaw 2026.3.13+'). This documentation is bundled in the UI but lives separately from any release process — there is no comment indicating when/how it should be updated, and no link from README/CONTRIBUTING.md telling maintainers to update it on release.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) move the markdown to a versioned doc file (e.g., docs/browser-attach-setup.md) and fetch/import it, or (b) add a comment near kReleaseNotesUrl noting it must be bumped on release and add an entry to CONTRIBUTING.md release checklist. Consider deriving the version string from package.json to avoid drift.

findings.title: Complex hooks/state machines undocumented (file-viewer, doctor, cron, telegram)
findings.description: Components like FileViewer, DoctorTab, CronTab, and TelegramWorkspace orchestrate non-trivial state machines (pendingRunSelectionId vs activeRunId vs selectedRunFilter in DoctorTab; multi-step wizard with localStorage persistence in TelegramWorkspace; routing draft + dirty detection in CronTab). The logic is correct but undocumented — there are no comments explaining state transitions, the polling-rate switch logic, or the localStorage cache invalidation strategy.
findings.recommendation: Add a short comment above each non-trivial useEffect explaining the invariant it maintains (e.g., 'Keep selectedRunFilter pointing at a real run unless we are tracking a pending run'). For TelegramWorkspace, document the storage-key strategy and onboarding step lifecycle near kSteps. For CronTab, comment hasUnsavedDetailChanges to explain the routing/prompt dirty contract.

findings.title: TelegramWorkspace localStorage keys/format undocumented
findings.description: lib/public/js/components/telegram-workspace/index.js persists onboarding progress and a workspace cache to localStorage via resolveStorageKey, with per-account suffixing and silent JSON parse failures. The schema of the persisted objects ({ step, groupId, groupInfo, ... } and the cache wrapper { cachedAt, data }) is implicit, and there is no doc describing the cache TTL/invalidation policy (saveTelegramWorkspaceCache stores cachedAt but it is never read).
findings.recommendation: Add a JSDoc @typedef for the persisted workspace state and cache payload. Add a brief comment explaining that cachedAt is informational only (or implement and document a TTL). Document the per-account key suffix rule ('default' uses bare key) which is non-obvious.

findings.title: Cross-package naming inconsistency (alphaclaw vs openclaw) not explained
findings.description: The codebase mixes 'alphaclaw' (kPluginId-style strings, ALPHACLAW_ROOT_DIR, ~/.alphaclaw, kPendingCreateAgentWindowFlag = '__alphaclawPendingCreateAgent', custom events 'alphaclaw:*', appBootCounter '__alphaclawSetupAppBootCount') with 'openclaw' (OPENCLAW_HOME, OPENCLAW_ROOT_DIR, openclaw CLI, github.com/openclaw/openclaw, docs.openclaw.ai). For new contributors this is highly confusing and there is no doc clarifying the relationship (rename in progress? two products? internal vs external naming?).
findings.recommendation: Add a short 'Naming' section to README.md or AGENTS.md explaining the alphaclaw/openclaw relationship and which name to use for new code. If a rename is in progress, capture it in an ADR (docs/adr/0001-naming.md) so the migration path is explicit.

findings.title: Custom event vocabulary undocumented
findings.description: The frontend uses several window-level custom events as a loose pub/sub bus ('alphaclaw:create-agent' dispatched/listened in app.js and agents-tab/index.js; postMessage with { google: 'success' | 'error' } in google/index.js). These are real public-ish APIs across components but are not enumerated anywhere. A new tab author would not know these exist.
findings.recommendation: Create docs/frontend-events.md (or a section in AGENTS.md) listing every custom window event and postMessage protocol used across components, with payload shape and producers/consumers. Reference it from each dispatch site via a one-line comment.

findings.title: Plugin event names ('llm_output', 'tool_result_persist') not contractually documented
findings.description: The usage-tracker plugin subscribes to api.on('llm_output', ...) and api.on('tool_result_persist', ...) and reads specific shapes from event/ctx (event.usage.input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite/total, event.sessionId, ctx.sessionKey, event.toolName, event.durationMs, event.message.{isError,ok,error}). This is the plugin contract, but there is no JSDoc @typedef or referenced doc describing the event payloads. Anyone writing another plugin must inspect callers to learn the shape.
findings.recommendation: Add @typedef LlmOutputEvent and @typedef ToolResultPersistEvent JSDoc blocks documenting fields used (or all fields), and link to a plugin authoring guide. Ideally publish a docs/plugin-api.md describing the api object (api.on, api.logger) and event catalog. The plan called out lib/setup/skills/gog-cli/ — same recommendation applies if that skill registers events.

findings.title: deriveToolSuccess heuristic lacks explanatory comment
findings.description: deriveToolSuccess() classifies a tool result as success or failure by checking event.error, message.isError, message.ok, and message.error. This duck-typing across multiple shapes is non-obvious and likely accommodates several producers (MCP results, AlphaClaw native tools, etc.). Without a comment explaining which producer maps to which field, future changes risk breaking the contract silently.
findings.recommendation: Add a short comment block above deriveToolSuccess listing each branch and the producer it targets (e.g., '// MCP tool results return { isError: true }; legacy tools return { ok: false } or { error: "..." }').

findings.title: No README/AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING.md content visible to validate top-level docs
findings.description: The plan listed README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, lib/setup/core-prompts/AGENTS.md, lib/setup/core-prompts/TOOLS.md, and lib/setup/skills/gog-cli/ as documentation focus areas, but the analyzed source contained only filenames (no body content) for those documents. I cannot evaluate whether install instructions are clear, contributor onboarding is sufficient, or skill docs are complete. This finding flags the gap so reviewers know to assess those files directly.
findings.recommendation: Re-run analysis with the actual contents of README.md, AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, lib/setup/core-prompts/*, and lib/setup/skills/gog-cli/* included so setup clarity, onboarding, and skill documentation completeness can be evaluated. Until then, treat the items above as code-side documentation findings only.

findings.title: Dependency manifest files (package.json, package-lock.json) not provided for analysis
findings.description: The PLAN identifies package.json, package-lock.json, .npmrc, patches/openclaw+2026.4.1.patch, scripts/apply-openclaw-patches.js, and .github/workflows/ci.yml as the focus files for dependency analysis. However, only application source code under lib/ was provided. Without the actual manifest, lockfile, .npmrc, patch file, and CI workflow contents, concrete dependency findings (pinned versions, CVEs, dev/runtime split, audit steps, patch-package drift) cannot be verified.
findings.recommendation: Re-run the dependency analysis with the manifest files included: package.json, package-lock.json, .npmrc, patches/openclaw+2026.4.1.patch, scripts/apply-openclaw-patches.js, and .github/workflows/ci.yml. These are required to assess pinning, lockfile hygiene, audit steps, and patch drift.

findings.title: Runtime dependencies inferred from imports — verify they are declared in package.json
findings.description: Source code imports several third-party packages: 'preact', 'preact/hooks', 'htm', 'wouter-preact', and 'marked' (used in lib/public/js/components/nodes-tab/browser-attach/index.js). These must be present as runtime dependencies in package.json (not devDependencies) since they appear in shipped UI code under lib/public/js. Without the manifest it cannot be verified whether each is correctly declared, pinned, and present in the lockfile.
findings.recommendation: Verify package.json declares 'preact', 'htm', 'wouter-preact', and 'marked' under 'dependencies' (not 'devDependencies'). Pin to specific minor versions or use caret ranges with a committed lockfile. Run `npm ls preact htm wouter-preact marked` to confirm resolution.

findings.title: Use of node:sqlite (experimental Node.js built-in) implies Node 22+ runtime constraint
findings.description: lib/plugin/usage-tracker/index.js requires 'node:sqlite' via `const { DatabaseSync } = require("node:sqlite")`. The node:sqlite module is experimental and only available in Node.js >= 22.5.0 (behind --experimental-sqlite in early releases, stabilized later). This creates an implicit engine constraint that must be declared in package.json 'engines' and enforced in CI to prevent silent runtime failures on older Node versions.
findings.recommendation: Add `"engines": { "node": ">=22.5.0" }` to package.json and `engine-strict=true` to .npmrc. Verify the CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml) tests on Node 22+. Document the Node version requirement in README. Consider feature-detecting node:sqlite at startup with a clear error message if missing.

findings.title: patches/openclaw+2026.4.1.patch indicates patch-package usage — drift risk
findings.description: The PLAN references patches/openclaw+2026.4.1.patch and scripts/apply-openclaw-patches.js. Patch files target a specific upstream version (2026.4.1). Whenever the upstream 'openclaw' dependency is bumped, the patch may fail to apply or silently mis-apply. Without seeing the patch contents and the apply script, the drift mitigation strategy (CI verification, version-check, postinstall hook) cannot be assessed.
findings.recommendation: Ensure CI runs the patch-apply step on every install and fails loudly on patch rejection. Pin the 'openclaw' dependency to exactly 2026.4.1 in package.json (no caret/tilde range) so the patch version matches. Add a postinstall script (`"postinstall": "node scripts/apply-openclaw-patches.js"`) and a CI assertion that the patched version equals the patch filename version.

findings.title: No automated dependency update tooling visible in provided files
findings.description: Neither a Dependabot config (.github/dependabot.yml) nor a Renovate config (renovate.json) was included in the provided file list. Without automated dependency updates, packages drift and CVEs accumulate. This is a maintainability concern for any long-lived Node.js project.
findings.recommendation: Add a .github/dependabot.yml configuration enabling weekly updates for the npm ecosystem and the github-actions ecosystem. Alternatively, configure Renovate. Ensure CI runs `npm audit --audit-level=high` and fails on findings.

findings.title: Polling pattern triggers redundant fetches across many components
findings.description: The DoctorTab uses three independent usePolling hooks (status, runs, cards) all polling at 2s when a run is in progress. Combined with similar patterns across general/watchdog/cron/usage tabs, this generates substantial network traffic. Each polling instance independently triggers HTTP roundtrips with no shared coalescing. With 5+ active panels polling every 2s, that's 150+ requests/minute just from one user.
findings.recommendation: Consider replacing aggressive 2s polling during active runs with SSE/WebSocket push updates (an sse.js client already exists). At minimum, share an api-cache layer so the three doctor polls don't issue redundant fetches when overlapping. Also gate polling behind document.visibilityState so background tabs don't keep polling.

findings.title: Synchronous SQLite writes in usage-tracker block event loop on every LLM/tool event
findings.description: writeUsageEvent() and writeToolEvent() use DatabaseSync (node:sqlite synchronous binding) on the hot path of every llm_output and tool_result_persist event. Each LLM completion triggers two sequential synchronous writes (insertUsageEventStmt.run + upsertUsageDailyStmt.run) which block the Node.js event loop. Under high agent throughput (multiple concurrent sessions, frequent tool calls), this can stall HTTP/WebSocket handling. There is no batching or write-behind buffer.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) wrap the two writes in a single transaction (BEGIN/COMMIT) to halve the fsync cost; (b) batch events in memory and flush every N ms / N events; or (c) move writes to a worker_thread. Given WAL+synchronous=NORMAL is already set, batching transactions of ~50 events would be the highest-impact fix.

findings.title: tool_events table missing index on timestamp
findings.description: The tool_events table has indexes on session_id and session_key but none on timestamp. Any analytics query filtering by time range (e.g., 'tool calls in last 24h') will require a full table scan. With high-volume tool usage this grows unbounded, causing read latency to climb linearly with row count.
findings.recommendation: Add `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tool_events_ts ON tool_events(timestamp DESC);` mirroring the usage_events index. Also consider a composite (session_key, timestamp) index for per-session timeline queries.

findings.title: App.js performs many regex matches and substring checks on every render
findings.description: App component re-evaluates location.startsWith() 6 times and runs location.match() 3 times on every render (every state change). For an SPA shell that re-renders frequently, these allocate new RegExp match objects each pass. Combined with the deeply-nested htm template literal that recreates the entire vdom tree, render cost compounds.
findings.recommendation: Use useMemo to compute route flags and parsed IDs derived from `location`. Move regex literals out of the render function so they aren't recompiled. This is minor per-render but accumulates with frequent re-renders driven by polling-based state.

findings.title: Cards filter and run-list slicing recomputed without proper memoization keys
findings.description: Doctor tab uses useMemo for cards filtering, but `displayRuns` is recomputed unconditionally on every render (line for `const displayRuns = pendingRun ? [pendingRun, ...runs] : runs;`). It then feeds visibleRuns/overflowRuns useMemo which depend on displayRuns identity (changes every render), defeating memoization. The .slice() runs every render even when runs are unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Wrap displayRuns in useMemo([pendingRun, runs]) so visibleRuns/overflowRuns memos remain stable when runs haven't changed. Same applies to allCards array spread.

findings.title: TelegramWorkspace localStorage writes on every state change
findings.description: The persistence useEffect serializes and writes the entire workspace state to localStorage whenever any of 7 dependencies (step, groupId, groupInfo, verifyGroupError, allowUserId, topics, accountId) change. localStorage.setItem is synchronous and triggers JSON.stringify on each call. During interactive flows (typing in inputs that update topics/allowUserId), this fires on every keystroke.
findings.recommendation: Debounce the localStorage save (e.g., 250ms) to coalesce rapid state changes during typing. Also avoid persisting transient fields like verifyGroupError that don't need cross-session persistence.

findings.title: BrowserAttachCard parses markdown on every mount via marked.parse
findings.description: marked.parse() runs inside useMemo with empty dependency array — parsed once per component instance. However, the static markdown string is the same across all users, so the parsing cost (~ms range) is incurred per mount rather than computed once at module load.
findings.recommendation: Move marked.parse() to module scope as a const so it runs once when the module is imported, not on each component mount. Trivial change for negligible but consistent improvement.

findings.title: Plan-targeted server files (chat-ws, watchdog, log-writer, sse, api-cache, usePolling) not provided for review
findings.description: The PLAN explicitly targets lib/server/chat-ws.js, lib/server/watchdog-terminal-ws.js, lib/server/watchdog.js, lib/server/system-resources.js, lib/server/log-writer.js, lib/public/js/lib/sse.js, lib/public/js/lib/api-cache.js, and lib/public/js/hooks/usePolling.js for performance-critical analysis (websocket backpressure, polling cache invalidation, sqlite query patterns, log writer I/O throughput, SSE stream handling). None of these were included in the source — only UI components and the usage-tracker plugin. The most impactful performance bottlenecks (WS lifecycle, log I/O, watchdog DB queries) cannot be assessed from what was provided.
findings.recommendation: Re-run analysis with the actual server-side WS, watchdog, log-writer, SSE, api-cache, and usePolling source files included. Findings against components-only code substantially under-represent the performance risk surface.

cross_cutting_insights: arch-000, arch-001, arch-002, qual-001, qual-006, qual-007, doc-002, doc-004, perf-003 all converge on the same root cause: lib/public/js/app.js conflates routing, state coordination, and shell layout. A single refactor (extract RouteSwitcher + useRouteParams + AppShellContext + remove window-flag pub/sub) addresses architectural, quality, documentation, and performance concerns simultaneously.

arch-003, arch-004, arch-005, doc-000, doc-001, doc-010 collectively define a missing 'plugin contract' surface. A single docs/plugin-api.md + shared contracts module with event constants, typedefs, lifecycle hooks (register/dispose), and host-provided paths/DB handles closes the architecture and documentation gaps together.

qual-011, doc-005, dep-004 are linked by version-string drift: hardcoded v2026.3.13 in UI markdown, patch filename openclaw+2026.4.1.patch, and lack of release-process automation. Centralizing version into package.json with build-time injection and a release checklist addresses all three.

sec-001 and arch-002 both stem from window-level postMessage/CustomEvent usage as a cross-component bus; introducing a typed event bus with origin validation fixes the security and architecture concerns together.

perf-001, arch-004, arch-005, qual-013 all concern the usage-tracker plugin's DB layer: synchronous writes, ad-hoc path resolution, no dispose hook, fragile migration. A holistic plugin-DB redesign (host-provided handle, transaction batching, PRAGMA-based migrations, lifecycle hooks) addresses performance, architecture, and quality together.

doc-008 (alphaclaw/openclaw naming) is a strong indicator of an incomplete rename. This likely amplifies the impact of arch-003 (plugin contract) and dep-004 (patch drift) because constants/env-vars/dep names may be in flux.
